ai.description: *Nyctibatrachus major* is a robust frog reaching 50–60 mm. It is brown with dark mottling and possesses prominent, fleshy, triangular toe discs and distinct, raised longitudinal skin folds on its back.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus major* is best distinguished by its distinctively elongated, pointed snout and the presence of prominent, fleshy, triangular toe tips compared to other species.
ai.habitat: The Malabar Night Frog inhabits evergreen forests and riparian zones in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 700 and 1,200 meters near rocky streams.
ai.behavior: The Malabar Night Frog is strictly nocturnal, remaining hidden in rock crevices or under leaf litter during the day before emerging to forage for insects at night.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus major* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 20–50 eggs on rocks near streams. They exhibit direct development, bypassing the free-swimming tadpole stage.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus major* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 700 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Malabar Night Frog emits a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "tink-tink" chirps, typically heard emanating from rocky streams within dense, humid evergreen forests.
